title: Carry the LSM peer context from SO_PEERSEC in ConsumerIdentity
description:
ConsumerIdentity should carry the peer's LSM security context, read via getsockopt(SO_PEERSEC), alongside whatever SO_PEERCRED gives.

NOT SELinux-specific. SO_PEERSEC dispatches through the kernel's LSM hook, so the active module fills in its own format:
  SELinux   user:role:type:level context
  AppArmor  profile name, e.g. snap.signal-desktop.signal-desktop
  Smack     Smack label
The daemon should treat it as an opaque string and not parse it. That covers RHEL in MLS mode, and equally Ubuntu and SUSE under AppArmor.

This is spec conformance, not a new idea. SPEC-HIA.md:199 and DESIGN.md:199 already specify the Linux chain as 'SO_PEERCRED (uid/pid) -> /proc/{pid}/exe -> binary hash -> AppArmor/SELinux label -> Flatpak/Snap app ID'. Only the first step is implemented.

Why it is worth more than the binary hash it supplements, per the project's own analysis at PRFAQ.md:68: a hash 'changes on every update' and the FAQ names re-enrolment after updates as the unsolved UX problem. An LSM profile name does not churn on update. For a confined app it is also assigned by policy rather than self-reported, so the process cannot change its own, which a binary path can be made to lie about.

Design note for whoever takes it: the field must be optional. An unconfined process on a system with no LSM has no context, and that absence is itself signal about attestation quality — it should weaken the derived pseudonym's standing rather than being treated as equivalent to a real label.

Broader shape, from the same conversation: ConsumerIdentity should not be a fixed pid/uid/gid struct. Solaris getpeerucred additionally yields zone, privilege set and, under Trusted Extensions, a sensitivity label; Windows yields a SID and Authenticode identity; Qubes has no local peer at all because the principal is a VM. Whatever shape persona-5s4b.41 lands should be extensible along that axis. Tracked separately as persona-vvs2 for the transport half.
